title: Medical disorders in pregnancy: thyroid disorders, intrahepatic cholestasis, AFLP and renal disease
subject: ss-obg
refs: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 53 (Hepatic Disorders), Ch 58 (Thyroid and Other Endocrine Disorders)
SMFM Consult Series #53: Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy
ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 148: Thyroid Disease in Pregnancy

steps.say: Maternal thyroid physiology alters substantially during normal pregnancy due to estrogen stimulation and human chorionic gonadotropin cross-reactivity. Rising estrogen elevates thyroxine-binding globulin, while peak chorionic gonadotropin in early gestation weakly stimulates the thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor, suppressing TSH levels transiently.
steps.tx: Estrogen-induced hepatic synthesis doubles circulating **thyroxine-binding globulin** (TBG), markedly expanding total T4 and T3 pools. In early pregnancy, peak concentrations of **human chorionic gonadotropin** cross-activate the **TSH receptor**, resulting in transient gestational thyrotoxicosis and physiological suppression of serum TSH below non-pregnant reference ranges.

steps.say: Diagnosing overt hypothyroidism in pregnant women requires prompt, assertive hormone replacement. Clinicians establish overt hypothyroidism by an elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone with suppressed free thyroxine, immediately initiating oral levothyroxine at 1.6 micrograms per kilogram daily.
steps.tx: Diagnosis of **overt hypothyroidism** is established by an elevated **serum TSH** exceeding pregnancy-specific trimester ranges (or > 4.0 mIU/L) with suppressed **free T4**. Treatment mandates immediate initiation of oral **levothyroxine** therapy (1.6 micrograms/kg daily), preventing impaired fetal neuropsychological development and spontaneous abortion.

steps.say: Treating maternal Graves disease requires choosing antithyroid medications carefully to avoid birth defects. Propylthiouracil is the preferred agent during organogenesis in the first trimester due to its low teratogenicity, before switching to methimazole in the second trimester to avoid maternal hepatic failure.
steps.tx: Active **Graves disease** in pregnancy requires careful antithyroid drug selection: **propylthiouracil** (PTU) is strictly preferred in the first trimester due to lower teratogenicity, switching over to **methimazole** in the second trimester to avoid severe PTU-induced maternal fulminant **hepatotoxicity** and acute liver failure.

left.title: Propylthiouracil (First Trimester)
points: Blocks thyroid peroxidase and peripheral T4 to T3 conversion
Avoids methimazole embryopathy (aplasia cutis, choanal atresia)
Black box warning: rare severe fulminant hepatotoxicity

right.title: Methimazole (Second/Third Trimester)
points: Switched at 14 to 16 weeks to spare maternal liver
Higher placental transfer; lower risk of maternal hepatitis
Dose titrated to keep maternal free T4 in upper-normal range

steps.say: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy is the most common gestational liver disorder, classically presenting in the late second or third trimester. Patients report intense, intractable pruritus concentrated predominantly over the palms of the hands and soles of the feet, worse at night.
steps.tx: **Intrahepatic cholestasis** of pregnancy classically presents in late second or third trimester with severe **pruritus** involving the **palms and soles**, typically devoid of primary dermatological lesions. The hallmark diagnostic test is elevated fasting **serum bile acids** exceeding 10 micromoles per liter.

nodes.label: Identify pregnant patient presenting with severe nocturnal pruritus of palms and soles
Obtain fasting total serum bile acid levels and liver function enzymes
Document total bile acids >= 10 micromol/L (mild: 10 to 39, severe: >= 40, peak: >= 100)
Initiate ursodeoxycholic acid therapy and schedule fetal surveillance

steps.say: Elevated maternal bile acids carry profound risks of sudden, unpredictable intrauterine stillbirth and spontaneous preterm labour. Ursodeoxycholic acid serves as the first-line medication, while maternal serum bile acid levels exceeding 100 micromoles per liter mandate delivery at 36 weeks gestation.
steps.tx: **Ursodeoxycholic acid** (UDCA at 10 to 15 mg/kg/day) acts as first-line pharmacotherapy, displacing hydrophobic cytotoxic bile acids. Delivery timing is dictated by bile acid severity: mild cases deliver at 37 to 39 weeks, whereas **bile acid levels** >= 100 micromol/L trigger **delivery at 36 weeks** due to catastrophic **fetal demise**.

steps.say: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy is a catastrophic obstetric emergency resulting from a fetal mitochondrial enzyme defect. Long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency in the fetus causes unmetabolized long-chain fatty acids to cross into the maternal circulation, causing microvesicular steatosis.
steps.tx: **Acute fatty liver of pregnancy** (AFLP) is a life-threatening late-trimester emergency linked to fetal **LCHAD deficiency** (long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase). Fetal fatty acids accumulate and flood maternal circulation, overwhelming the liver and provoking widespread **microvesicular steatosis**, coagulopathy, and acute hepatic failure.

left.title: Pathophysiology of AFLP
points: Fetal homozygous G1528C mutation in LCHAD enzyme
Maternal heterozygous liver overwhelmed, microvesicular fat

right.title: Emergency Obstetric Action
points: Immediate stabilization of coagulopathy and hypoglycemia
Urgent prompt delivery regardless of gestational age
Postnatal newborn screening for LCHAD deficiency

steps.say: Swansea diagnostic criteria establish the clinical diagnosis of acute fatty liver of pregnancy without requiring invasive biopsy. Validated diagnosis requires meeting six or more clinical and laboratory features, including severe vomiting, abdominal pain, hypoglycemia, hyperuricemia, encephalopathy, and coagulopathy.
steps.tx: The validated **Swansea criteria** establish the diagnosis of AFLP if 6 or more features are present: vomiting, abdominal pain, polydipsia, encephalopathy, elevated bilirubin (> 14 micromol/L), profound **hypoglycemia** (< 4.0 mmol/L), hyperuricemia, leukocytosis, coagulopathy, and diffuse **microvesicular steatosis** on imaging or biopsy.

nodes.label: Assess patient in third trimester with nausea, vomiting, and epigastric tenderness
Evaluate 14 Swansea criteria (glucose, bilirubin, PT/INR, uric acid, ammonia)
Document presence of 6 or more Swansea criteria confirming AFLP
Initiate IV dextrose, cryoprecipitate, and immediate emergency delivery

steps.say: Chronic kidney disease impairs maternal hemodynamics and escalates the risk of superimposed preeclampsia and preterm delivery. Women with severe baseline renal impairment whose serum creatinine exceeds 2.5 milligrams per deciliter experience accelerated kidney decline, requiring dialysis planning and multidisciplinary care.
steps.tx: Pre-existing **chronic kidney disease** in pregnancy carries high risks of superimposed preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction. When **baseline serum creatinine** exceeds 2.5 mg/dL (or GFR < 30 mL/min), there is accelerated irreversible **renal decline**, necessitating intensive hemodynamic monitoring and pre-emptive **hemodialysis** planning.
